message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total), which sits just above the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and stays within the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, with no funds transferred out of the account. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth-quarter and full-year results, which I verified against both Apple's newsroom release and the SEC 10-K after a search result from a lookalike "filings mirror" site reported clearly fabricated numbers ($361.2B revenue, $79.4B net income, $5.12 EPS) that I discarded: actual FY2024 total net sales were $391,035 million (up from $383,285 million), net income $93,736 million, diluted EPS $6.08, and operating income $123,216 million, with Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion up 6% year over year — and notably the FY net income and EPS figures were depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge, meaning underlying profitability was stronger than the headline decline suggests. Recent news flow was neutral-to-constructive, with shares trading roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively given the absence of a strong near-term catalyst and the stock's already-full valuation.
